subject: Early performance touchpoints — recommendation and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Early performance touchpoints — recommendation and next steps

Hi Lauren and Mina,

I want to flag an early but persistent performance concern with one of my ICs on Platform (I will avoid naming here until HR advises on next steps). Over the last ~8 weeks I've observed several recurring issues: missed sprint commitments, lack of timely communication on blockers, and deliverables that require repeated rework. I started informal coaching in March (1:1s + paired work) and I drafted a short feedback summary attached.

My ask: can HR confirm recommended next steps for a pre-PIP coaching path (documentation expectations, cadence, and any paperwork templates we should use)? From a manager standpoint I propose the following initial plan: 

- 1:1 weekly focused on two concrete outcomes (deliverable quality, proactive updates)
- Weekly written touchpoint summarizing expectations and owner actions (use attached template)
- Clear success criteria with measurable checkpoints at weeks 2 and 6
- Escalation triggers if improvements not observed (examples in the doc)

I attached my initial feedback notes and a blank weekly touchpoint template. I want to be careful here — goal is improvement and clarity, not immediate escalation. Happy to sync this afternoon if that helps.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Platform
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: initial_feedback_notes.docx (docx, 38 KB)]
[Attachment: weekly_touchpoints_template.xlsx (xlsx, 12 KB)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early performance touchpoints — recommendation and next steps

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments — helpful to see the concrete examples. Quick thoughts:

- I agree with a 6-week coaching window but suggest an initial 30-day checkpoint to triage and adjust expectations.
- Make the weekly touchpoint short and action-oriented (3 bullets: what was tried, blockers, commitments for next week).
- For success criteria, tie them to observable outcomes (e.g., PR acceptance rate, on-time delivery of feature X) rather than subjective language.

Let's avoid naming in email — glad you looped HR. I can join the first coaching 1:1 as a neutral observer if you think that would help calibrate tone.

If HR confirms the templates, I'd like to finalize and send the first-week expectations note to the IC by Tuesday.

-Lauren
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early performance touchpoints — recommendation and next steps

Thanks for the context, Jordan — and for keeping this confined to the manager/HR loop. I reviewed the attached notes and your proposed cadence. Recommended HR protocol for a pre-PIP coaching sequence: 

1) Documentation & Notice:
   - Manager documents the specific behaviors/metrics and provides the IC a written "Coaching Plan" (use the template).
   - Plan must include: start date, checkpoint dates (Day 14 and Day 42), measurable success criteria, and available support resources (mentorship, pairing time, learning allowance).

2) Meeting Cadence & Witnessing:
   - Weekly 1:1s with a brief written summary after each meeting. HR prefers the manager to copy HR on the Week 1 and Week 4 summaries.
   - If manager invites a leader to witness the conversation, inform the employee in advance.

3) Confidentiality & Tone:
   - Keep content factual and coaching-focused. Avoid attribution of intent.

4) Escalation & Next Steps:
   - If checkpoints are missed, manager escalates to HR to discuss formal PIP conversion.

I've attached the official pre-PIP guidance and a sanitized example of a completed touchpoint. Also note: if you plan to involve an additional leader in 1:1s, we should document that in the Plan.

I'll be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10:00 if you'd like to walk through the language.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pre-pip-guidelines.pdf (pdf, 95 KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early performance touchpoints — recommendation and next steps

Thanks Mina — that template and the schedule look good. I booked your 10:00 slot to review wording (calendar invite sent).

Two quick clarifications I want to capture before we finalize:
- Do we need to inform the IC that HR will be copied on the Week 1 summary, or is it fine to copy HR without calling it out?
- For the success criteria, would HR prefer specific numeric targets (where feasible) or a mix of qualitative+quantitative?

My inclination: we should tell the IC that HR will receive written summaries (transparency helps) and use numeric targets where reasonable but not forced.

I will update the attached template with the 30-day and 6-week checkpoints and send a draft to you both after our sync.

-Jordan

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Early performance touchpoints — recommendation and next steps

Jordan, Lauren — thanks again for the quick turnaround this week. Follow-ups from our call: 

- Transparency: please tell the IC that HR will receive the Week 1 summary. This should be framed as support and record-keeping.
- Success criteria: where objective measures exist, use them (PR turnaround time, number of rework cycles, on-time milestone delivery). For behavior/communication items use observable examples (e.g., responded within 24 hours with status; added JIRA ticket updates).
- I reviewed your updated template in Drive and left a couple of inline suggestions (link below).

Action items: 
- Jordan: send the Week 0 (kickoff) expectations note to the IC by EOD Monday and copy HR. Use the attached sanitized example as a guide.
- Lauren: join the first 1:1 as neutral observer next Tuesday.
- Mina: I'll prepare an HR checklist and a short note to attach to the Coaching Plan that outlines reasonable accommodations/training options.

Link to updated doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/eng/feedback/2026-05-rd1

I'll follow up with the formal HR checklist early next week.

Mina Haddad
Senior HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference
